description: Quip is a NATIVE multi-platform app (QuipMac SwiftUI macOS, QuipiOS SwiftUI iOS, QuipLinux Rust) — there is NO npm/jest/web surface. The phone renders one-tap answer chips for interactive CLI prompts (Claude/Codex/shell) by parsing the live terminal text with the pure cross-platform detector in Shared/NumberedPromptDetector.swift. Today detectInlineOptions(in:) only recognizes BRACKETED inline choices ('Continue? [yes/no]') — keyed on lastIndex(of: ']') — so parenthesized prompts ('Continue? (yes/no)', 'Pick? (1/2/3)'), same-line trailing prompt cursors, and several common CLI choice words render NO chips, leaving the user unable to answer from the phone. This PRD hardens the detector to cover the real prompt shapes these tools emit, WITHOUT admitting prose false-positives, and keeps fingerprint(in:) in lockstep so the Mac/iOS answer-revalidation ('Prompt changed — not sent') never drops a valid answer. HARD CONSTRAINTS (do not violate): (1) Edit ONLY Shared/NumberedPromptDetector.swift (logic) and QuipiOS/Tests/NumberedPromptDetectorTests.swift (tests). No other files. (2) xcodebuild is the ONLY compile/test oracle — SourceKit / IDE 'No such module XCTest' or 'Cannot find type X in scope' (WindowManager, ManagedWindow, TerminalApp, TerminalStateDetector) are SPURIOUS cross-file noise; ignore them. (3) The iOS detector test gate is: xcodebuild test -project QuipiOS/QuipiOS.xcodeproj -scheme QuipiOS -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17 Pro' -only-testing:QuipiOSTests/NumberedPromptDetectorTests -derivedDataPath build → output contains '** TEST SUCCEEDED **'. The Mac compile gate is: xcodebuild build -project QuipMac/QuipMac.xcodeproj -scheme QuipMac -destination 'platform=macOS,name=My Mac' -derivedDataPath build-mac → '** BUILD SUCCEEDED **' (the Shared change must compile on Mac too; do NOT run the Mac TEST action — its bundle fails to load on a Team-ID signing mismatch, unrelated to code). (4) NEVER weaken an existing prose-rejection test — every story must keep ALL existing NumberedPromptDetectorTests passing (no false positives). (5) detect/detectInlineOptions and fingerprint MUST stay in agreement for every new shape (a detected prompt has a non-nil, stable fingerprint). (6) Stay on the ralph/smart-answer-detector-v2 branch; never push; never git add -A — add only the two changed files plus prd.json and progress.txt. (7) Do NOT touch signing, TCC, entitlements, or any .xcodeproj/.entitlements/Info.plist.

userStories.title: Detect parenthesized inline choice prompts
userStories.description: As a Quip user, I want '(yes/no)' and '(1/2/3)' inline prompts to render answer chips on the phone, so I can one-tap answer the many CLIs that use parentheses instead of brackets.
acceptanceCriteria: detectInlineOptions(in:) recognizes a parenthesized choice group '( … / … )' with the SAME guards already applied to '[ … ]': trailing-only after the close paren (space/./?/)/:), a '/' separator inside, a choice cue ('?' or a cue word) before the group on the same line, charset-safe tokens, and at least one digit/anchor-word token.
Detected: 'Continue? (yes/no)' → ["yes","no"]; 'Approve which? (all / 1 / 2 / none)' → ["all","1","2","none"]; 'Proceed? (y/n)' → ["y","n"].
Rejected (still nil): 'printf(a/b) returns void.' (no cue), 'Pick? (main / dev)' (no anchor token), 'The ratio (1/2) is small.' (no cue).
Bracketed detection is unchanged — all existing inline bracket tests still pass.
New tests added to QuipiOS/Tests/NumberedPromptDetectorTests.swift cover the detected and rejected parenthesized cases above.
iOS detector gate passes: xcodebuild test ... -only-testing:QuipiOSTests/NumberedPromptDetectorTests prints '** TEST SUCCEEDED **'.
Mac compile gate passes: xcodebuild build ... QuipMac prints '** BUILD SUCCEEDED **'.
userStories.notes: Added parseChoiceGroup(open:close:) + validateChoiceTokens() helpers; parseInlineChoiceLine now tries bracket then paren through the SAME guards. 57 tests pass, Mac BUILD SUCCEEDED.

userStories.title: fingerprint() tracks parenthesized prompts in lockstep
userStories.description: As a Quip user, I want a parenthesized prompt to produce a stable fingerprint so my queued answer isn't dropped with 'Prompt changed — not sent' when the terminal text reflows.
acceptanceCriteria: fingerprint(in:) returns non-nil for every parenthesized prompt that US-001's detectInlineOptions detects (the inline fingerprint branch covers parens, not just brackets).
For a parenthesized prompt, fingerprint is STABLE across surrounding ANSI escape codes and a trailing cursor/whitespace change (same value before and after).
fingerprint changes when the option tokens change (e.g. '(yes/no)' vs '(yes/no/cancel)') and when the choice text changes.
A prose string with parentheses but no prompt (e.g. 'call foo(a/b) now.') yields a nil fingerprint (agrees with detect returning nil).
New tests assert fingerprint non-nil+stable, fingerprint-vs-detect agreement, and the prose-nil case for parenthesized inputs.
iOS detector gate passes: xcodebuild test ... -only-testing:QuipiOSTests/NumberedPromptDetectorTests prints '** TEST SUCCEEDED **'.
Mac compile gate passes: xcodebuild build ... QuipMac prints '** BUILD SUCCEEDED **'.
userStories.notes: Refactored detectInlineOptions to wrap private inlineChoiceMatch(in:) returning the normalized matched line + tokens. fingerprint's inline branch now hashes the whole normalized line ('inline:'+line), so it changes when the question text changes (not just option tokens) yet stays stable across ANSI/trailing-cursor/whitespace. Same match func ⇒ detect/fingerprint agreement guaranteed. 63 tests pass, Mac BUILD SUCCEEDED.

userStories.title: Recognize a same-line trailing prompt cursor after the choice
userStories.description: As a Quip user, I want prompts that print the input cursor on the SAME line as the choice ('Continue? [yes/no] › ', 'Proceed? (y/n) ❯') to still render chips, since not every CLI puts the cursor on a new line.
acceptanceCriteria: After the closing bracket/paren, a single trailing prompt-marker glyph (one of: ❯ › » > $ # :) optionally surrounded by spaces is tolerated as benign trailing punctuation (in addition to the existing space/./?/)) — for BOTH bracket and paren groups.
Detected: 'Continue? [yes/no] ❯' → ["yes","no"]; 'Proceed? (y/n) > ' → ["y","n"]; 'Which? [1 / 2 / 3] ›' → ["1","2","3"].
Still rejected: a glyph that is part of prose after the bracket, e.g. 'See [docs](url) › home.' stays nil (the existing cue/anchor guards still apply).
fingerprint stays in agreement (non-nil) for these same-line-cursor prompts.
All existing detector tests still pass (no regression to the trailing-period/question/paren cases).
New tests cover the same-line-cursor detected cases (bracket + paren) and at least one prose rejection.
iOS detector gate passes: xcodebuild test ... -only-testing:QuipiOSTests/NumberedPromptDetectorTests prints '** TEST SUCCEEDED **'.
Mac compile gate passes: xcodebuild build ... QuipMac prints '** BUILD SUCCEEDED **'.
userStories.notes: Added inlineTrailingAfterClose Set<Character> = [space . ? ) : ❯ › » > $ #]; parseChoiceGroup's after-close guard now checks membership in that set instead of an inline allSatisfy. Same-line cursor glyphs pass for BOTH bracket+paren; prose after the close still carries letters → token charset guard rejects. fingerprint stays non-nil (same inlineChoiceMatch path). 67 tests pass, Mac BUILD SUCCEEDED.

userStories.title: Lock v2 behavior with a real-transcript regression matrix
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want one table-driven test mapping realistic Claude/Codex/shell prompt strings to their expected chips (or nil), so the v2 detector behavior is pinned and future edits can't silently regress a real prompt shape.
acceptanceCriteria: A new table-driven test in NumberedPromptDetectorTests.swift asserts detectInlineOptions for a matrix of >= 10 realistic inputs covering: bracket + paren, digits + words, yes/no shorthand, trailing period/question/colon/cursor, a multi-line prompt with a cursor line below, AND >= 3 prose-bracket/paren NON-prompts that must return nil.
Every 'expected chips' row also asserts fingerprint(in:) is non-nil; every 'expected nil' row asserts fingerprint is nil — proving detect/fingerprint agreement across the whole matrix.
The matrix includes at least one input that exercises each capability added in US-001..US-003.
The FULL detector suite passes (not just the new test): xcodebuild test ... -only-testing:QuipiOSTests/NumberedPromptDetectorTests prints '** TEST SUCCEEDED **' with 0 failures.
Mac compile gate passes: xcodebuild build ... QuipMac prints '** BUILD SUCCEEDED **'.
